State Parks

Every state park, forest, historic site, and recreation area in the 50 state park systems — 3,520 in all, each linked to its page on the state’s own website — plus the maximum RV length of 210,518 individual campsites.

State ▲▼ Park ▲▼ County ▲▼ Official Website ▲▼
No parks match that search.

How this works. Every campsite below carries the maximum length its own reservation system allows — 132,717 state-park sites in 42 states and 77,801 federal sites on Recreation.gov. Enter your rig and see which campgrounds have sites long enough. In the states that explain their numbers, the listed length has to hold everything on the pad, tow vehicle included — so the tow box is on by default. Always confirm the exact site when you book.

State ▲▼ Campground ▲▼ Sites that fit ▲▼ RV sites ▲▼ Longest ▲▼ Pull-through ▲▼ Full hookup ▲▼ Check-in Check-out Book
Nothing fits those settings. Try a shorter rig, fewer hookup needs, or turn off pull-through.

“Pull-through” and “Full hookup” count only the sites that fit. Check-in and check-out are per campground for federal sites (Recreation.gov) and the state’s standard campsite times for state parks (“Varies” where the state sets them park by park) — see the RV rules tab for each state’s source. Some systems don’t publish hookups or driveway type per site (Florida, Louisiana and Vermont publish no hookups; most US eDirect states publish no driveway type), so those sites drop out when you ask for them — they may still have them.

Read this first. No state publishes a single system-wide maximum RV length — the limit is set per campsite and lives in each state’s reservation system. Where a state does say how length is measured, it measures the whole rig on the driveway: Oregon and Wisconsin say so outright, and Arkansas and Missouri require everything to fit on the spur or pad. Treat “Not stated” as “the state does not publish it,” not as “no limit” — and assume your tow vehicle counts unless a park tells you otherwise.

Measured from the state reservation systems

Every bookable RV-capable campsite in 42 states, pulled from the platforms that run their reservations — 132,717 sites across 1,551 parks, each carrying its own maximum vehicle length, plus hookups and driveway type where the system publishes them. Cabins, yurts, tent-only, walk-in, boat-in, equestrian and day-use units are excluded, as are marina docks and parking that some systems sell with a vehicle length attached.

Federal campgrounds, by state
